as_told.title: Townsend Brown at the Institute of Field Physics, Wright Field sponsorship
as_told.place_text: Institute of Field Physics, North Carolina

plain: The physicist Bryce DeWitt, who helped found the study of quantum gravity, ran an Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina that Michels says was also funding the high-voltage gravity experiments of a researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown at the same time. Michels tells it across several episodes and adds details as he goes: that Wright Field, an Air Force base, sponsored a 1957 conference of top physicists at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill while the university backed Brown's antigravity work, that the Air Force general Curtis LeMay was a sponsor, that there is a video of Brown popping champagne in the lab, and that the institute was a CIA outpost studying antigravity. If so, mainstream physics and secret gravity research would have shared the same rooms and money.
